title: Corrugated cardboard
instruction: Use the ridged layers of a shipping box as your main building material. Cut, fold or laminate them.

title: Paper
instruction: Make paper do the work. Fold, roll, pleat or layer ordinary sheets into a useful structure.

title: Scrap wood
instruction: Give a wooden offcut another job. Make it a useful part of your contraption.

title: Discarded packaging
instruction: Turn a clean box, carton or packing insert into the main structure of your build.

title: Paperboard tubes
instruction: Build around one or more paperboard tubes. Use their hollow shape, or cut and reshape them.

title: Craft sticks
instruction: Use craft sticks as the main structural pieces. Connect them into something that works.

title: Bottle caps
instruction: Make clean bottle caps an essential part of your build. Explore their rims, circles and small size.

title: Plastic bottles
instruction: Give a clean plastic bottle a new purpose. Use its body, neck or flexible walls in your build.

title: Fabric scraps
instruction: Make fabric an essential working part. Fold, stretch, tie or stitch your scraps into shape.

title: String or yarn
instruction: Use string or yarn to carry a load, connect parts or transmit motion. Put tension to work.

title: Thin craft wire
instruction: Bend thin craft wire into a useful structure or moving part. Give those lines a job to do.

title: Rubber bands
instruction: Put rubber bands to work. Use their stretch, grip or stored energy as a key part of your build.

title: Clothespins
instruction: Use wooden clothespins as working parts. Try their jaws, spring or wooden halves.

title: Egg cartons
instruction: Turn a clean egg carton into a useful structure. Explore its cups, ridges and folding lid.

title: Corks
instruction: Use corks as key parts in your invention. Explore their grip, buoyancy or rounded shape.

title: Aluminum foil
instruction: Make foil do useful work. Fold, crumple or layer it into a shape that helps your invention.

title: Fallen twigs
instruction: Gather fallen twigs and build with their natural shapes. Join them into a useful structure.

title: Three rescued objects
instruction: Choose three clean objects headed for the trash. Give all three a useful role in one contraption.

title: Lever
instruction: Pivot a bar on a support. Use movement at one end to lift, push or move something at the other.

title: Wheel and axle
instruction: Connect a wheel to a shaft so they turn together. Use their rotation to help accomplish the mission.

title: Pulley
instruction: Run a cord over a turning wheel. Use it to redirect a pull or help move a load.

title: Counterweight
instruction: Use one weight to balance or move another part. The balancing weight must do useful work.

title: Ramp
instruction: Use a sloped surface to guide motion or raise an object gradually. Make the slope do useful work.

title: Wedge
instruction: Push a tapered piece between surfaces. Use its shape to lift, separate or hold something.

title: Screw
instruction: Use a threaded connection to turn rotation into straight-line movement or a holding force.

title: Cam and follower
instruction: Turn a shaped wheel against a follower. Use its changing profile to lift or move the follower.

title: Crank and slider
instruction: Connect an off-center crank pin to a guided slider. Turn the crank to create back-and-forth travel.

title: Linkage
instruction: Join rigid pieces with pivots. Use the connected pieces to guide or transfer movement.

title: Meshing gears
instruction: Make toothed wheels engage. Use one gear to turn another and help accomplish the mission.

title: Belt drive
instruction: Loop a belt around two wheels. Use the belt to carry rotation from one wheel to the other.

title: Ratchet and pawl
instruction: Let a catch engage a toothed wheel or strip. Allow motion one way and resist it the other way.

title: Spring return
instruction: Store energy in a spring or elastic part. Release it to bring a moving part back toward its start.

title: Gravity feed
instruction: Arrange parts so gravity supplies the motion. Guide objects toward a useful destination.

title: Pendulum
instruction: Hang a weight from a pivot and let it swing. Use the repeated motion to help with your mission.

title: Spool and cord
instruction: Wind or unwind a cord around a drum. Use the changing cord length to move another part.

title: Flexible hinge
instruction: Join two parts with a bendable strip. Make movement happen by bending the joint.

title: Lift a small object
instruction: Raise a small object from a lower level to a higher one. Let your mechanism do the lifting.

title: Cross a gap
instruction: Move a small object from one side of a gap to the other. Keep it out of the space below.

title: Deliver a message
instruction: Carry a written or drawn message from its starting point to a waiting recipient.

title: Reveal something hidden
instruction: Keep an object or message concealed. Operate your contraption to bring it into view.

title: Sort by size
instruction: Separate a mixed collection into at least two size groups. Make the contraption help decide.

title: Dispense one at a time
instruction: Hold several similar objects. Release just one during each operating cycle.

title: Hold it in position
instruction: Keep an object in a chosen position without holding it yourself. Show that it stays put.

title: Protect something fragile
instruction: Build a way to protect a fragile object from a small bump. Use a harmless stand-in first.

title: Draw a repeating pattern
instruction: Move a drawing tool or a surface to make a pattern repeat. Let the mechanism guide it.

title: Bring a creature to life
instruction: Give an imagined creature a convincing movement. Make it nod, flap, crawl or express a mood.

title: Give a visible signal
instruction: Make a clear visual change that someone can recognize from across a table.

title: Make a sound
instruction: Create an intentional sound when your contraption operates. Make it happen again on demand.

title: Compare two weights
instruction: Show which of two small objects is heavier, or whether they balance. Use the same test for both.

title: Slow a moving object
instruction: Make an object move more slowly than it would without your contraption. Compare both runs.

title: Catch and release
instruction: Catch a small moving object, hold it briefly, then release it through your mechanism.

title: Fold into less space
instruction: Make a useful structure that folds into a smaller form. Open it again and show it still works.

title: Operate from a distance
instruction: Control an action from beyond arm's reach. Keep your hands away from the part doing the job.

title: Move two things together
instruction: Use one input to make two separate parts move at the same time. Give both parts a visible job.
